messages.subject: Adjacency Matrix
parts:
I'm running into some strange results (i.e. the CAR model provides a completely opposite direction of the coefficient of interest compared to the multilevel unstructured model and the no random effects model), and I'm wondering if there is technique to check that the adjacency matrix is indeed accurate. These results are quite strange, so I'm a bit perplexed. My model is structured thusly:

mod.inla.preterm.car <- inla(Preterm ~ NO2_LUR + MED_HHI + NO2_LUR:MED_HHI + agem + as.factor(edum) + as.factor(racem) + as.factor(prencare) + f(id,NO2_LUR,model="besag", graph="socal.adj"),family="binomial",data=my.dat.sample)


Thanks,
Eric

parts:
I have tried the stripped down model as suggested and this is the result:

mod.inla.preterm.car <- inla(Preterm ~  f(id, model="besag", graph="socal.alt.adj"),family="binomial",data=my.dat.sample)

Fixed effects:
               mean     sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant    mode kld
(Intercept) -2.4218 0.0102     -2.442  -2.4218    -2.4018 -2.4218   0

When I include a random intercept with the covariate ("NO2_LUR") of interest I obtain the following (note: this is in the direction we would expect):
mod.inla.preterm.car <- inla(Preterm ~ NO2_LUR + f(id,model="besag", graph="socal.alt.adj"),family="binomial",data=my.dat.sample)

Fixed effects:
               mean     sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant    mode kld
(Intercept) -2.6899 0.0813    -2.8494  -2.6900    -2.5302 -2.6901   0
NO2_LUR      0.0119 0.0036     0.0049   0.0119     0.0189  0.0119   0


When I include the random slope with the covariate of interest I obtain the following (note: this is in the opposite direction of what we would expect):
mod.inla.preterm.car <- inla(Preterm ~ NO2_LUR + f(id,NO2_LUR, model="besag", graph="socal.alt.adj"),family="binomial",data=my.dat.sample)

Fixed effects:
               mean    sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant    mode kld
(Intercept) -1.2910 0.022    -1.3342  -1.2910    -1.2478 -1.2910   0
NO2_LUR     -0.0395 0.001    -0.0415  -0.0395    -0.0376 -0.0395   0

So I'm still perplexed.

Best,
Eric

On Fri, 2014-04-04 at 11:49 -0700, Eric Coker wrote:

> mod.inla.preterm.car <- inla(Preterm ~ NO2_LUR + f(id,NO2_LUR, model="besag", graph="socal.alt.adj"),family="binomial",data=my.dat.sample)
>
> Fixed effects:
> mean sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant mode kld
> (Intercept) -1.2910 0.022 -1.3342 -1.2910 -1.2478 -1.2910 0
> NO2_LUR -0.0395 0.001 -0.0415 -0.0395 -0.0376 -0.0395 0

the model='besag' has default constr=TRUE, meaning that it sums to zero.
so it does not make much 'sense' to have both NO2_LUR+f(id,NO2_LUR,...),

try

Preterm ~ f(id, NO2_LUR,model='besag', constr=FALSE, graph = "...")
